app.title: gitma_CANSpiN (Streamlit GUI, version 1.7.0)
app.summary: A person registers a remote CATMA annotation project by giving it a label and an access token, then picks the project's folder from the list the token can reach and saves it. Saved projects can be edited, deleted or chosen from a dropdown. Once a project is chosen, the tool pages in the sidebar menu become available. On the exporter page the person marks one stretch of the text as the segment to process, and its character offsets are shown as JSON. The analyzer and manipulator pages are only headings so far.

task.text: Keep a set of connections to remote annotation projects and choose one to work on, then mark the stretch of text that later processing should use.

data.text: Saved records of remote annotation projects (a label, a folder name and an access token), plus a text with one marked segment given by its character offsets.
data.item: a CATMA project: a folder of documents and annotation collections, reached with an access token

stage.text: keeping annotation projects in order after annotating in CATMA, before exporting and analysing the annotations

mechanism.text: A sidebar main menu switches between pages and keeps the tool pages disabled until a project is chosen. The projects page uses modal forms that fetch the folder list from the remote backend, plus a dropdown that sets the current project and shows its details. The exporter page shows the text in a span labeler, and the marked segment is echoed as JSON.

field.text: managing CATMA text-annotation projects in the digital humanities

workflow.name: connect to a remote project and mark the segment to process

steps.here: The Create dialog asks for a project label and a CATMA access token. It downloads the names of the folders that token can reach, and Save stays disabled until one folder is picked from the radio list.

steps.step: keep the saved collection in order
steps.here: Edit reopens the dialog filled in with the chosen project's label, token and folder. Delete removes it. Every change is written to a local projects JSON file.
A dropdown of saved projects sets the current project, and success boxes show its name, folder and token.

steps.step: switch to the tool that does the next job
steps.here: Choosing a project enables the AnnotationExporter, AnnotationAnalyzer and AnnotationManipulator buttons in the sidebar main menu.

steps.step: select a stretch and label it with a category
steps.here: On the exporter page a text labeler shows the text with a 'text_borders' span, and the person drags to set where the segment starts and ends.
The labeler's output is printed as JSON: the span's start and end character offsets and its text.

distinctive: The access token decides what can be chosen: the folder list comes live from the CATMA backend, and authentication or connection failures are shown in place of the list.
The tool pages stay locked in the main menu until a project is chosen, so every later step works on one named remote project.
The segment to process is a single 'text_borders' span given in character offsets. It is meant to cut away header metadata or narrow the text to one chapter before export.
Saved projects, tokens included, persist between sessions in a local JSON config file.
The exporter page runs on seeded placeholder text, and the analyzer and manipulator pages are empty headings.
